SELECT id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY ROLLUP(id)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: ROLLUP creates five ordinary id groups, including physical NULL, plus one grand-total row; grouping provenance cannot be inferred from NULL alone.

cases.sql: SELECT id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY CUBE(id)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Single-key CUBE produces the same two grouping levels as ROLLUP; physical NULL and subtotal are separate row occurrences.

cases.sql: SELECT GROUPING(id), COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY ROLLUP(id)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: GROUPING(id) returns a non-null 0 for every present grouping key (including physical NULL), 1 only for the generated grand total.

cases.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: ROW_NUMBER produces 1..N by position; equal ORDER BY keys do not identify a particular physical peer.

cases.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY amount) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: PARTITION BY id resets row numbers for every group, including the physical NULL group; two id=1 rows get {1,2}.

cases.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY amount) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: ROW_NUMBER over amount has six distinct output positions but tied amount=10 has no portable physical assignment.

cases.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY amount, id) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Additional ORDER BY id does not distinguish two duplicate (id,amount)=(1,10) physical instances.

cases.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY amount NULLS LAST) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Explicit NULLS LAST controls NULL-key position, not identity of equal amount=10 peers.

cases.sql: SELECT RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: RANK uses one-plus preceding row count; three amount=10 peers have rank 2 and next rank is 5.

cases.sql: SELECT DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: DENSE_RANK counts earlier distinct sort groups, so the amount=20 group has rank 3 rather than 5.

cases.sql: SELECT NTILE(3) OVER (ORDER BY amount) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: NTILE(3) on six records yields two occurrences per bucket, exactly {1,1,2,2,3,3}.

cases.sql: SELECT PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: PERCENT_RANK=(RANK-1)/(N-1); rank gaps and tied peer equality must be preserved.

cases.sql: SELECT CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY amount) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: CUME_DIST counts current and preceding tied occurrences over total N, giving 1/6,4/6,5/6,1.

cases.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: ROWS previous/current uses physical adjacent positions; same-key rows carry identical amount so output bag is peer-stable.

cases.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY id RANGE BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: RANGE 1 PRECEDING includes all equal numeric-key peers; NULL id forms its own peer frame.

cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY id GROUPS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: GROUPS 1 PRECEDING includes the entire current peer group, making COUNT(*) >=1 for every output row.

cases.sql: SELECT AVG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY amount ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM orders
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Partitioned AVG ignores SQL NULL and returns NULL for a partition containing no non-NULL amount.

cases.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) OVER w FROM orders WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Named window resolves ORDER BY id with UNBOUNDED PRECEDING ROWS; no finite row count assumption in portable type law.

cases.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM orders QUALIFY rn = 1
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER=1 selects one value rn=1; the chosen physical id=1 duplicate is not stable under ties.

cases.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM orders QUALIFY rn = 1 AND id > 0
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: QUALIFY rn=1 AND id>0 rejects every non-first row and NULL id under SQL three-valued logic.

cases.sql: SELECT o.id, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY c.id) AS n FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.id = c.id QUALIFY n > 1
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Two orders id=1 times two customers id=1 produce four distinct join instances; only id=2 pair fails COUNT OVER >1.

cases.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM orders QUALIFY rn > 1
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: QUALIFY rn>1 retains exactly five rank values and rejects the single first peer occurrence (physical peer identity ambiguous).

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1 returns value bag {1,2} for six input ids under DuckDB NULL-last semantics; four candidate occurrences are not emitted.

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY id FETCH FIRST 2 ROWS WITH TIES
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Original FETCH WITH TIES must remain semantically distinct from LIMIT despite DuckDB rejecting the original spelling. TASK-191 owns parser/runtime.

cases.sql: SELECT TOP 2 id FROM orders ORDER BY id
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Original TOP 2 is not independently executed by DuckDB; parser acceptance alone proves no physical output bag. TASK-191 owns.

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY amount LIMIT 2
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: LIMIT 2 under amount ordering picks id=4 first and one peer with amount=10; which physical peer survives is under-specified.

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (10)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: BERNOULLI sampling is a probabilistic subset, not a fixed value bag; source occurrence subset and 0..6 bounds only.

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (10)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Repeated original BERNOULLI SQL remains a distinct named sampling test, with no deterministic selected occurrences.

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (10)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: SYSTEM sampling depends on block/session sampling laws; a fixed population is not a fixed selected bag.

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (10) REPEATABLE (7)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: REPEATABLE(7) does not prove cross-engine seed/session stability or a universal selected physical bag.

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (10)
cases.reviewed_semantic_basis: Repeated SYSTEM SQL retains a separate original test identity but shares conditional subset laws.
